correctness.rationale: Exact character-ring reconstruction gives \(\operatorname{Sym}^0(\rho_4)=\rho_1\), \(\operatorname{Sym}^1(\rho_4)=\rho_4\), \(\operatorname{Sym}^2(\rho_4)=\rho_6\), \(\operatorname{Sym}^3(\rho_4)=\rho_8\), and \(\operatorname{Sym}^4(\rho_4)=\rho_3\oplus\rho_7\). Combining the mixed sectors with the six traceless logical-operator representations yields first positive-degree overlaps \((2,2,2,4,2,2)\). An independent character-inner-product reconstruction reproduced the vector. For the full one-loss error set, Knill–Laflamme products have total degree at most two, so only depth four is symmetry-forced scalar; \(\mathcal E_{2,2}\) contains \(\rho_3\), blocking a symmetry-only two-loss guarantee.
residual_risks: The conclusion is only a symmetry guarantee; seed-specific coefficients may vanish even when a non-scalar intertwiner is allowed.

originality.rationale: The depth vector is mathematically correct, but the final scientific content is a direct finite corollary of the motivating paper’s own equivariant-QEC theorem, complete \(2O\) character data, six-choice Table III, and its low-degree sector tables. The source already displays the key contrasts: for \(\rho_1\oplus\rho_2\), \(\mathcal E_{1,1}\) carries a non-scalar logical \(Z\); for \(\rho_3\), the same low-degree blocks carry no logical error and the first \(X,Y\) sector occurs at \(2,2\). The remaining four depth entries follow by routine character inner products from the same published table. Under the implication/corollary rule, absence of the exact six-number vector does not make this original.
